Counsel for Applicant :- Dinesh Kr. Chaudhary
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Vidyarthi,J.
1.
Heard Sri Dinesh Kumar Chaudhary, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Ravish Chandra Mishra, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the records.

2. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
82 of 2023, under Sections 323, 363, 366, 376 I.P.C., registered at Police Station Pachpedwa,
District Balrampur.
3. The aforesaid case has been registered on the basis of an F.I.R. lodged on 17.02.2023 stating that the applicant had enticed away the informant's minor sister.
4. In the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. she stated that she knows the applicant for the past four years.
5. In the medico legal examination of the victim no mark of any injury has been reported on any part Maajid Hussain @ Majid vs State Of U.P. Thru.Prin.Secy. Deptt. Of ...

her body and her aged has been opined to be 19 years.

6. In the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. she stated that the applicant is aged about 17 years and she made some contradictory statements, like she did not know the applicant and that now the applicant has declined to marry her.

7. In the affidavit filed in support of bail application it has been stated that the applicant is innocent,
he has been falsely implicated in the present case and he has no criminal history.
8.
The learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail but he could not dispute the aforesaid aspects of the matter.

9. Having considered the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the fact that both the applicant and the victim are young persons; that in her initial statement the victim had stated that she knows the applicant for the past four years and in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. the victim has stated that she does not know him but she further stated that now the applicant has declined to marry her, coupled with the fact that the victim is a major and no mark of any injury has been found on any part of her body and also that the applicant has no previous criminal history and he is languishing in jail since 24.02.2023 and without making any observation,
which may affect the merits of the case, I am of the view that the aforesaid facts are sufficient for making out a case for enlargement of the applicant on bail in the aforesaid crime.
10.
Accordingly, this bail application stands allowed.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.
(Subhash Vidyarthi, J.) Order Date :- 22.5.2023
